title: lia-wang-private-deploy-scratchpad-2026-03-05
content:
Daily scratchpad - Private deploy field notes (ACME Health proof-of-concept)
Date: 2026-03-05
Owner: Lia Wang

High level status:
- In customer VPC, prepping air-gapped + KMS integration.
- Installer (helm + operator) mostly working in staging; hitting network/firewall and KMS access issues in customer env.
- Next on-deck: finalize image registry mirror, validate KMS permissions, and test model download/quantized weights load without outbound.

Immediate TODOs (quick list):
- [ ] JIRA-1234: Create and validate ECR mirror + signed images for air-gapped (owner: Lia)
- [ ] JIRA-1256: Confirm KMS key policy with security (owner: Miguel)
- [ ] JIRA-1260: Run install with --helm-set useHostPath=true to validate NFS fallback (owner: Riley)
- [ ] Add automated smoke test that hits /v1/health and runs a small token-generation (owner: Lia)

Environment reminders (customer-specific):
- VPC CIDRs: 10.10.0.0/16 (private), 10.11.0.0/24 (bastion/management).
- No outbound internet allowed from worker subnets; only via proxy in management subnet.
- KMS is AWS-Managed, must use key alias acme-prod/llm-kms, cross-account access required.
- Customer requires FIPS-compliant TLS and HSM-backed key (note from security call 2026-03-03).
- MTU on network is 1400 (seen earlier mismatch with default 1500 causing big packet drops).

Install notes / commands tried:
- Helm values used on staging: 
  -- set image.repository=registry.redwood-internal/serve 
  -- set image.tag=2026-02-28-quant 
  -- set persistence.storageClass=gp2 
  -- set routing.fallbackModel=redwood/llama-2-small

- For air-gapped: we mirrored images to a local Harbor instance. Steps:
  1) pull images from registry.redwood-internal:443
  2) docker save -> transfer to customer via secure jumpbox -> docker load -> push to harbor.acme.internal/serve
  3) update helm values: image.repository=harbor.acme.internal/serve, image.pullSecret=acme-pullsecret

- KMS testing: attempted client-side encryption with AWS SDK using assumed role. Error: AccessDenied on Encrypt call.
  - logs: "User: arn:aws:sts::222222:assumed-role/RedwoodDeployRole is not authorized to perform: kms:Encrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:333333:key/xxx"
  - action: need updated key policy to allow the cross-account role and on-prem host principals. Contact: security@acme.com and link to JIRA-1256.

Blockers and hypotheses:
- Blocker 1: KMS policy missing cross-account principal for the deploy role -> blocks model artifact encryption/decryption during startup. Hypothesis: once policy applied, services will be able to decrypt cached model shards.
- Blocker 2: Air-gap registry cert chain not trusted by container runtime on nodes -> image pull failures. Quick fix: add CA cert to /etc/docker/certs.d/harbor.acme.internal/ca.crt via cloud-init.
- Blocker 3: MTU mismatch causing grpc connections to drop on larger payloads (batch size > 4). Workaround: set GODEBUG=tcpadr=1? (investigate). Immediate workaround: reduce batch size to 2 in runtime config.

Observability / logs to check if things fail again:
- kube-system events: kubectl -n redwood get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
- pod logs for controller: kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/serve-controller -c manager --since=1h
- model-worker logs (on GPU node): sudo journalctl -u redwood-model-worker -f

Config snippets to copy into helm values (notes to self):
- registryMirror:
  url: "https://harbor.acme.internal/serve"
  pullSecret: "acme-pullsecret"
- kms:
  enabled: true
  provider: aws
  region: us-west-2
  keyAlias: "alias/acme-prod-llm"
- network:
  mtu: 1400
  useHostNetwork: false

Quick troubleshooting checklist (when customer calls):
1) Verify node date/time sync (NTP) - mismatched time has caused cert validation fails before.
2) Confirm CA installed on nodes for internal registry.
3) Re-run helm install with --debug and paste output into slack thread for engineers to triage.
4) If KMS fails, try a minimal Encrypt/Decrypt using aws kms ciphertext CLI as the assumed role to isolate IAM vs network.

Notes from last remote session with ACME on 2026-03-04:
- They prefer we operate behind their NATing proxy for egress. We need to support proxy config for image pulls and KMS STS calls.
- Ops asked for a short runbook for rotation of model keys (how we re-encrypt KV cache after key rotate). Add to runbook.

Follow-ups (meetings/emails):
- 2026-03-06 10:00 PST - Call with ACME infra team to finalize KMS policy (invite: Miguel, Lia).
- 2026-03-07 09:00 PST - Validation window to run air-gapped install (Riley to coordinate).

Random TODO notes to self:
- Add small script to check MTU across all nodes (ssh -> ip link show dev eth0 | grep mtu) and fail early in installer.
- Add explicit helm value to force batch_size in runtime: runtime.batchSize=2 for slow networks.
- Save a copy of the CA chain at s3://redwood-internal-share/acme/ca-chain.pem (ask infra for write access).

Links & refs:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/ACME+Health+Private+Deploy
- Slack thread: #private-deployments (search "acme health install")
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/helm-charts/pull/87 (registry mirror support)

Notes to self (less formal):
- Keep deploy footprint small for first run. One small model worker GPU (A10G) + 2 CPU workers for API. If memory pressure, move to quantized weights.
- If the customer insists on HSM, we may need to run a small K8s-side HSM proxy. Check with security on supported HSM vendors.

End of scratchpad for today.

-- Lia
